Reddit is a grand experiment. It calls itself the front page of the internet, and a place where anyone can post interesting content. But in practice, due to the way moderation and subreddits are structured, people don't have to actually discuss things with each other. They can retreat into their own little walled garden of thought, joined by like-minded individuals, and are free to shun any dissenting opinions.

And sure, that's fine in theory, but humans don't work very well in those environments over time. Each sub turns into a hivemind for that particular topic, a positive feedback loop of shared experience and vaguely circlejerky logic built up over time, by people who hide in their garden and shun the rest of the site as something foreign or perverse. So instead of having big discussions that foster mutual understanding and compromise, it becomes a forum for massively parallel radicalization, where points are scored by yelling louder and longer than your opponent, and each can retreat to their hugbox when exhausted. And in a lot of ways this is a problem of the internet as a whole.

When you give people who have preconceived biases an echo chamber to converse with like-minded people, and then give them fake internet points for parroting their compatriots in thought, it's not hard to see that the absolute worst trains of thought known to man will distill as a natural consequence.

I'm a bit delirious this late at night, so I hope this isn't too rambly, but the answer to this question is deceptive, and a lot more difficult than it appears on the surface. Do you double down on democracy and tear down the walls that keep negativity out of sight? Or do you sacrifice your principles (like reddit did) and ban people and/or subs only after they cross some vague threshold of incivility? Because we can't pretend that haters don't exist, and in a real democracy they have to be able to say their piece, and then get voted into oblivion. That'll be especially hard here considering how many of us are too new to have any downvoats at all.

Each sub turns into a hivemind for that particular topic, a positive feedback loop of shared experience and vaguely circlejerky logic built up over time, by people who hide in their garden and shun the rest of the site as something foreign or perverse.

And when you propose the decision to either double down on democracy or submit to a "benevolent dictator", that might be a false dichotomy. But I think I would have to choose the former in this case. Make all speech, whether hateful or productive, equally visible. And the community should, if it is decent enough, reevaluate itself. Hate speech should be visible so that it can be acknowledged. We should be the judge of what content is best.

Soccer fans! Play 3v3 VS Landon Donovan, Brian Ching, and Stuart Holden at the Austin Aztex game on 8/1

The Austin Aztex are pleased to announce that Brian Ching, Stuart Holden, and Landon Donovan, all founders of Helm Soccer, will be special guests at the Austin Aztex game on August 1, 2015 as part of their three-day stay in Austin for their Helm Soccer School.

“We are thrilled to bring our inaugural Helm Soccer camp to Austin,” said Landon Donovan. “The Austin Aztex have been instrumental in making our first camp a reality and we are excited to be able to support the Aztex as well as the Aztex Soccer Foundation in helping to serve the Austin community.”

The Helm Soccer Schools camp welcomes all levels of players to learn under the guidance of Donovan, Holden, and Ching. The Austin camp, which runs from July 31 to August 2, are day camps open to children from ages 10-18, both girls and boys. Fans can find more information on the Austin Helm Soccer School on their website.

As part of their mission, these soccer legends have chosen to partner with the Austin Aztex and give the chance for three lucky fans to play a 3v3 game against Brian Ching, Stuart Holden, and Landon Donovan during halftime of the Austin Aztex vs. Portland Timbers II game on Saturday, August 1 at Kelly Reeves Athletic Complex. Funds raised from the auction will benefit the Aztex Soccer Foundation. Helm Soccer’s mission is to enhance the lives of America’s youth by maximizing their soccer potential and giving back to local and national charities. The live online auction for the 3v3 game will begin Tuesday, July 14 at 10 a.m. CDT.

“We are proud to partner with such a great organization that shares common goals of using soccer to give back to the community,” said Aztex Soccer Foundation President David Markley. “It is a privilege to have three players of such caliber choose to support our foundation in this way.”

HELM will also auction off additional autographed items at the game, with bidding commencing online and ending at the end of halftime. All proceeds raised from these items will also benefit the Aztex Soccer Foundation. All items, including the 3v3 match, will be posted on www.austinaztex.com.
